title: Classes and objects
bridge: A **class** is a blueprint; an **object** is one thing made from it with `new`. Fields hold its data (usually `private`), a **constructor** sets them up, and methods (not `static`) work on that object's own data through `this`.

notes: A class inside Example, to keep it in one file.
A method that guards its data.
Two objects, each with its own kg.

exercises.title: A bank account
exercises.prompt: Make class Account with a private double balance, a constructor Account(double opening), deposit(double amount), withdraw(double amount) that returns false (and changes nothing) if the money isn't there, and getBalance(). Negative or zero amounts throw IllegalArgumentException.

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<Double>) () -> { Account a = new Account(50); a.deposit(25); return a.getBalance(); }).get()
((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Account a = new Account(50); boolean ok = a.withdraw(80); return ok + " " + a.getBalance(); }).get()
((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Account a = new Account(50); boolean ok = a.withdraw(20); return ok + " " + a.getBalance(); }).get()

hints: withdraw: if (amount > balance) return false; balance -= amount; return true;

exercises.title: toString
exercises.prompt: Make class Item with a name and a quantity (int), a constructor Item(String name, int qty), and toString() returning like "maize x 3". Add take(int n) that lowers the quantity but never below 0.

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Item i = new Item("beans", 5); i.take(2); return i.toString(); }).get()
((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Item i = new Item("kale", 2); i.take(9); return i.toString(); }).get()

hints: public String toString() { return name + " x " + qty; }

quiz.q: What's the difference between a class and an object?
choices: A class is the blueprint; an object is one thing made from it
quiz.why: new Plot("North") makes an object from the Plot class.
